› Write a 600 word story about a lighthouse.

  The light was more than a mechanism; it was a heartbeat. Each rotation, a
  brilliant, silent drumbeat against the relentless drumming of the rain. It
  spoke a language that transcended spoken words—a language of safety, of
  warning, of unwavering persistence.

  Tonight, the storm was a beast. It didn't merely blow; it roared, clawing at
  the lantern room glass. Waves, immense and angry, hammered the base of the
  tower, sending plumes of spray high into the air, where they dissolved in the
  halo of the beam. The wind shrieked, a thin, tormented voice that seemed to
  whisper ancient tragedies to the stout stone.

  Elara trimmed the wick, her movements economical and practiced. She had grown
  used to the battle—the screech of the gulls (which were now merely tormented
  specters), the smell of salt
